fail_closed_monitoring_review.review_objective: Audit the operational risks of automated process restarts and specify strict fail-closed recovery invariants for prospective paper evaluation.

risks_of_naive_automatic_restarts.name: Rapid-Fire Restart Thrashing & IP Blacklisting
risks_of_naive_automatic_restarts.description: If an unhandled exception is caused by an invalid API token, network partition, or vendor rate-limiting, an OS-level daemon supervisor (e.g. systemd/NSSM) blindly restarting every 5 seconds will hammer the provider API, resulting in temporary or permanent IP bans and account suspension.

risks_of_naive_automatic_restarts.name: Duplicate Order Replay & Double Fill Exposure
risks_of_naive_automatic_restarts.description: If a crash occurs after an order was transmitted to the broker/simulator but before the execution fill was committed to disk, an automatic restart that re-evaluates the strategy could re-transmit the same buy/sell order, doubling position size or causing unauthorized margin borrowing.

risks_of_naive_automatic_restarts.name: Corrupted State & Deserialization Cascades
risks_of_naive_automatic_restarts.description: If a host power failure or abrupt kill leaves a JSON journal file partially written, an automatic restart attempting to parse malformed JSON could enter an infinite crash loop or miscalculate portfolio cash.

risks_of_naive_automatic_restarts.name: Stale Market Data Execution
risks_of_naive_automatic_restarts.description: If vendor feeds freeze or fail to update, an auto-restarted runner could calculate signals and place orders against yesterday's closing prices during a market crash.

invariant_1_persistent_incident_lock.mechanism: Physical `INCIDENT_LOCK` file written to persistent storage containing UTC timestamp, error code, stack trace, and SHA-256 HMAC integrity signature.
invariant_1_persistent_incident_lock.behavior: Runner startup routine immediately inspects disk for `INCIDENT_LOCK`. If detected, the process halts immediately with exit code 99 and logs a fatal error without opening network connections or placing orders.

invariant_2_manual_authorization_require.rule: Automated daemons, scripts, or supervisors are STRUCTURALLY FORBIDDEN from clearing an `INCIDENT_LOCK`. Clearing the lock requires a human operator to inspect root cause and execute an explicit cryptographic reset command.

invariant_3_deterministic_order_id_dedup.rule: Every outbound order generates a deterministic client order ID: `UUIDv5(namespace, session_date + ticker + target_shares + nonce)`. Broker sandbox/simulator must reject duplicate client order IDs to prevent replay.

invariant_4_double_entry_pre_reconciliat.rule: On every startup or recovery, the complete disk event journal is replayed through `DecimalAccountingOracle`. If balance sheet identity `Cash + Receivables + Equities == Total Equity` does not match to exact Decimal precision, startup aborts into `INCIDENT_LOCK`.

invariant_5_stale_data_circuit_breaker.rule: If incoming market data timestamp is older than max allowable latency (e.g. > 18 hours for daily EOD bars, or > 15 minutes for intraday bars), trading signals are inhibited and alert is dispatched.

invariant_6_isolated_external_watchdog.rule: External monitoring (e.g. Healthchecks.io / Uptime Kuma) acts strictly as a passive dead-man's switch receiving periodic pings. The watchdog has ZERO broker credentials, ZERO ability to generate orders, and ZERO ability to clear incident locks.

fail_closed_monitoring_review.environmental_restriction: NO SUPERVISORS, WATCHERS, OR DAEMONS HAVE BEEN INSTALLED OR STARTED IN THIS REPOSITORY.
